row.name: Southwest Ridge via Tombstone Pass
row.description: Follow Tombstone Creek to Tombstone Pass, traverse to the cirque below the summit and climb the southwest ridge to the summit block. The block itself is a short 5.4 crack on the south side. Class 2 to the summit block, which is Class 4.

row.name: Direct North Buttress
row.overview: A varied mix of cracks and faces. Heading left along a ledge below an orange lichen bulge leads to the "Triple Cracks", which seemed the hardest physically; the alcove has loose rock beneath it, yet the narrow crack over it is solid. Farther up, a 5.10b dihedral begins stiff before easing, and a big fixed cam sits in the offwidth/chimney past it. Near the top, gendarmes and pillars crowd a ridge where 4th and 5th class mix.

row.name: North Ridge Direct
row.overview: Three steep pitches reach 5.10-, after which the ridge is fourth-class and easy fifth-class. P1 (160', 5.8): from the left, traverse over ledges to a belay where steep orange cracks begin. P2 (160', 5.10-): hand-width splitter over a steep bulge, ending at a horn belay (#3 and a double sling). P3 (120', 5.10-): finger-width crack on the left cuts the bulge and reaches the ridge. P4: 400' along the ridge, then 800' of easier scrambling (2nd to 3rd class) finishes at the summit.
row.approach: From the Pine Creek trailhead, follow the trail past Pine Lake and Upper Pine Lake to Honeymoon Lake, then continue to Granite Park. Above the lake, cut southwest cross-country up and over Royce Pass to reach the Royce Lakes basin. Go around to the west shore of the largest Royce Lake; the orange cracks that lead up to the ridge are easy to pick out and serve as a guide.
row.descent_text: The route finishes on the summit of Royce Peak, after a long stretch of third and fourth class and easy fifth class along the ridge. A walk-off to the south leads down from there.

row.name: North Face
row.overview: Follows the prominent couloir up the middle of the peak. The first ascent stayed mostly on the rock walls, crossing between them to avoid snow and ice. After heavy winters snow persists in the couloir into fall and turns to blue alpine ice at about 50 degrees. The top-out squeezes via a natural bridge and lands near the summit. The way down depends on the approach. If returning to Cox Col or Lake Italy, take the south slopes (loose, class 2). If returning to Second Recess, take the Northwest ridge, also called the Glacier Route (class 2). The approach is one of the longest walk-ins for ice in the Sierra.

row.name: North Arete
row.overview: P1 (5.6): slab cracks, depending on snowline. P2 (5.8): flake crack on the left. P3 (5.7): flakes up and right; the way may be hard to find. Pitches 4 and 5 (easy 5th): crest to a ledge under the final steep offwidth. P6 (5.8, crux): the awkward crack. P7 (easy 5th): a tunnel to the other side. Then either join the Northeast Ridge or keep to the arete crest to the summit ridge, a pitch or two of scrambling. Mantle the summit block.

row.name: North Face
row.overview: A trail to the trailhead via Ruby Lake is the way out: descend the East Couloir route, passing Mills Lake. The climb crosses the glacier to a clear couloir centered on the north face, ascends it (about 40 degrees) until a solid rock cap stops it, then veers right onto gentler terrain, mostly 3rd class, to reach the flat top before the summit itself.
row.approach: Start at Mosquito Flat and hike the trail toward Mono Pass. From the pass go left (west) up an easy slope to the ridge top and scramble down the far side into the Fourth Recess, the trickiest part of the approach. Descend a broad, low-angle scree chute, turn south and go up the recess, passing Snow Lakes, to reach the glacier under the north face.
row.descent_text: The route ends on the summit plateau, crossed to the summit. The normal way off is the East Couloir route, passing Mills Lake to Ruby Lake where the trail back to the trailhead is picked up. Parties camped in the Fourth Recess can instead go back down the north face.
